newsitem.title: THAILAND: General Motors seeks 10 pct of Asian market.
newsitem.headline: General Motors seeks 10 pct of Asian market.

text.p: General Motors Corp said on Friday its $750 million Asian car project here is part of the company's long-term plan to raise its share of the Asia-Pacific market to 10 percent from 4.8 percent in 1996.

GM vice president Phil Johnston told diplomats and reporters gathering at the Eastern Seaboard Industrial Estate, where its car plant is being built, that the company will export up to 80 percent of 100,000-150,000 Opel Asian cars to be produced from here annually.
The GM plant, 117 kms east of Bangkok, is due to start production in early 1999.
Johnston said GM will export the German-designed lower medium sedan to key Asian and regional markets including Japan and Australia.

He said GM sold 624,000 vehicles in Asia-Pacific last year. "...By the year 2006, Asia Pacific will outperform growth in both North America and Europe to become the largest automobile market," he said.

Johnston said the giant auto maker chose Thailand over rival Philippines as the site of its Asian car plant because the country's auto industry has the largest potential growth in the region after Japan and South Korea.

"Thailand's economic policies have remained consistent despite frequent changes of government...we believe the fundamentals of the economy remain strong and it should maintain healthy, sustainable growth for the forseeable future," he said.
